editorial.headline: Specialised Construction Beyond the Ordinary Build
editorial.standfirst: A broad specialist-construction category, open nationally to full foreign ownership and not blocked for PMA registration in Bali.
editorial.body:
This activity covers specialised construction work requiring particular expertise or equipment where the job falls outside the more specifically classified construction groups. Its terrain is unusually wide: waterproofing and damp-proofing, including storage tanks; building dehumidification; shaft sinking; industrial chimneys and ovens; work at height requiring climbing skills and related equipment; and underground works. It also reaches into the practical fabric of public infrastructure, from road safety barriers, traffic signs and road markings to noise walls and street furniture.

The scope is equally attentive to highly technical construction and preservation. It includes conservation, repair and restoration of cultural-heritage buildings; concrete, asphalt and granular paving; construction drilling and pressure cement injection; structural concrete; and post-tensioned concrete work. Fire-resistant construction is also within the activity, including furnaces, annealing installations, flares and incinerators for residential and non-residential buildings as well as other civil structures. The common thread is not one building type or material, but the specialist capability needed to execute demanding work safely and precisely.

Registration is open across every stated business scale: Mikro, Kecil, Menengah and Besar. Nationally, the PMA position is TERBUKA, with a foreign-ownership ceiling of 100%. In plain terms, the record permits full foreign ownership at the national level. That openness should be read alongside the nature of the activity itself: this is a category for businesses undertaking specialised construction operations, rather than a generic label for routine building work.

Bali adds an important operational distinction without reversing that national position. The province permanently blocks PMA registration for all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI activities island-wide. This activity is not blocked by that moratorium: at the Besar scale, its OSS risk is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi, reflected in the Bali status `OK_or_HIGHER_RISK`. For foreign investors, the decisive point is not a local exclusion but whether the project sits at the large-scale risk level identified by OSS.
